summary_of_change:
Fluor Corporation is navigating a complex operational restructuring characterized by substantial liquidity generation from asset sales alongside uneven underlying contracting performance. Over the trailing four quarters, top-line trajectory transitioned from $3.4B in Q3 2025 (burdened by a $653M revenue reversal in Energy Solutions due to adverse arbitration) to $4.2B in Q4 2025, $3.6B in Q1 2026, and $4,329.0M in Q2 2026, establishing an annualized revenue run-rate of $17,316.0M. Segment profit execution has been volatile, rebounding to $170M in Q2 2026 from just $8M in Q1 2026 and $120M in Q4 2025, with reported gross margin at 4.1%.

Operational volume units show total project backlog expanding to $26.9B, aided by $6.1B in quarterly new awards (89% reimbursable), bringing total backlog composition to 85% reimbursable. This shift significantly mitigates lump-sum procurement exposure. However, execution friction remains visible: Mission Solutions absorbed a $98M legal ruling charge alongside a $71M segment loss earlier in the cycle, while Urban Solutions experienced cost growth on the Gordie Howe International Bridge and Americas mining engagements. Operating cash flow stood at -$317M in Q2 2026 due to a discrete $357M tax settlement from NuScale share monetization, following $110M in Q1 2026 and $286M in Q3 2025.

The balance sheet represents a major pillar of support, holding $3,043.0M in cash and marketable securities against $1,072.0M in total funded debt, yielding net cash of $1,971M ($14.70 per share across 134.1M shares). Management has deployed this liquidity into share repurchases, executing $816M in buybacks through the first half of 2026 against a full-year target of $1.4B, while continuing to manage remaining legacy project closeouts.
